column1: # Accepted differences between our demuxers and ffprobe. Tab-separated, one rule per line:
#   format   field   scope   rule   follows   reason
# format: our container format name or *.   field: pts dts duration size pos key hash count or *.
# scope:  * | kind=video|audio|subtitle|data | codec=<ffprobe codec name> | file=<substring of the path>
# rule:   ignore | ffprobe-na (ffprobe prints N/A) | ours-na (we report no value) | tolerance=N (ticks of ffprobe's time base)
# follows: which side follows the specification (ours, ffprobe, neither), or n/a when it is a definition choice.
# A rule only excuses a difference; it is counted separately in the reports. Add rules with the experiment that justifies them.

column6: ffprobe reports the start of the Block element (id and size included); we report the start of the frame payload, as the packet's source range must be the bytes handed to the codec.
The last packet's duration: ffprobe replaces it (parser frame length for MP3/AC-3/AAC, or the edit's end); the sample table states the value we report (docs/isobmff.md).
duration-from-codec: ffprobe derives a duration the file does not store from the codec's frame length; ours stays unknown (docs/matroska-differential.md).
last-block-duration-differs: the last block's stored BlockDuration is shorter than the codec's frame; ffprobe reports the frame length (docs/matroska-differential.md).
inexact-timebase: when TimestampScale does not divide 10^9 ours are exact nanosecond ticks and ffprobe's integer time base rounds (docs/matroska-differential.md).
dts-unknown-for-video: Matroska stores presentation times only; ffprobe prints the pts as the dts (docs/matroska-differential.md).

Positions and sizes were compared separately with the packetset command.

edit-list-in-fragmented-file: the edit [0+0] has segment_duration 0, which ISO/IEC 14496-12 8.6.6 reads as the whole track in a fragmented file; ffprobe drops the first 47 table samples (docs/isobmff.md).
truncated-copy-straddling-sample: ffprobe lists the sample straddling the end of the corpus copy; ours stops before it (docs/isobmff.md).
mp3-in-quicktime-one-byte-samples: the table lists the MP3 as 17.6 million one-byte samples; ffprobe reframes them by MP3 frame headers, which needs a parser at the packet level (docs/isobmff.md).
video-parser-frame-timing: packet 0 lasts 6210 in the sample table (it alternates 6210/6120); ffprobe takes the parser frame timing (docs/isobmff.md).
realaudio-deinterleave: ffprobe de-interleaves RealAudio cook/ra blocks into 280-byte packets; ours delivers the stored 1400-byte blocks (docs/matroska-differential.md).
realvideo-timestamps: ffprobe derives RealVideo frame times from the stream (azumi.mkv has blocks at 80 and 81 ms where it reports 40 and 80); ours is the block time (docs/matroska-differential.md).
ffprobe reports the start of the data packet the payload sits in; we report the start of the payload bytes, and none for an object reassembled from several payloads (docs/asf.md).
duration-from-codec: ffprobe derives an audio or video packet duration from the bit rate or frame rate; the file states none per packet (docs/asf.md).

reorder-capable-video: ffprobe prints no PTS for video whose decoder may reorder frames (WMV3 here); the payload's presentation time is the one value the file states and we report it as both PTS and DTS (docs/asf.md).

damaged-tail: the last 10 video objects of this file have inconsistent fragment positions (ffprobe logs 'packet fragment position invalid'); ffprobe and we keep different parts of them (docs/asf.md).

damaged-data-stops-ffprobe: packet 8 of this deliberately damaged file has invalid length fields; ffprobe stops after 7 packets, we report asf.packet-* defects, skip the damaged packets and keep reading (docs/asf.md).

declared-packet-size-wrong: File Properties states 1250-byte packets but the data packets after the second sit 2048 bytes apart; ffprobe resynchronises on packet headers, we follow the declared size and report asf.packet-* defects (docs/asf.md).
picture-in-id3-attribute: the cover art sits in an ID3v2 tag stored in the 'ID3' attribute; we hand out that attribute as a binary native tag until the ID3 layer reads it (docs/asf.md).

dvr-ms-elementary-stream-chunks: DVR-MS stores raw MPEG elementary stream chunks and a time-code extension in the replicated data; ffprobe re-frames the chunks with its stream parsers and reads the extension (docs/asf.md).

duration-from-file-size: these ten-frame files carry no Xing/Info frame, so ffprobe estimates the duration from the file size and the first frame's bit rate, which counts tag bytes (the APE and ID3 tags are 4 to 40 percent of a 4 to 6 KB file); ours counts the frames (10 x 1152 samples at 44.1 kHz = 0.261224 s).
